TWO FINDINGS. (1) THE DEFINITION IS INCOMPLETE AS STATED: the bigraded ideal is given as I_{m,n} := ((q;q)_m * P_n(q,z)), but P_n(q,z) is never defined in the block, and it is the only thing carrying the z-direction of the bicompletion. (q;q)_m is the standard cyclotomic generator, so the q-side is determined and the z-side is not; a reader cannot reconstruct the inverse limit. Proposed fix: define P_n (presumably the z-Habiro cyclotomic generator from def:z-habiro-ring) or cite it. (2) WALL-SIDE MISMATCH: the block closes with the boilerplate 'Archimedean specialisation. What follows sits on the archimedean side of the substrate wall ... specializes them to real-valued observables at q_0.' Nothing follows -- it is the last paragraph -- and the object defined is an inverse limit of quotients of Z[q^{+-1}, z], manifestly pre-archimedean with no real-valued observable anywhere in the block. The banner appears to have been applied mechanically. Proposed fix: remove it, or move it to whichever downstream block does the q_0 evaluation.
